prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE exceptionally polished desktop website design comp, 1536x1024 landscape: the first viewport of a page plus the beginning of the next section. A real web layout, edge to edge, no device frame, no browser chrome.

The attached reference images are screenshots of the SAME website's already-built homepage. Carry over exactly: the header (the script wordmark "Birdcar" at left in a forward-leaning connected brush script; at right the nav "How I work", "Selected work", "Writing" and a compact canary-yellow pill button "Book a free Walkthrough →" with ink text), the pale daylight ground #edf3f0, near-black ink #0b141a, the heavy, tight, confident grotesk (Mona Sans) for every heading and body line, white pill tags with soft shadows, canary yellow #f7c848 only on actions and things in motion, teal #5fb8bf only for a resolved state, and the premium matte isometric miniature render style (soft studio daylight, fine architectural-model detail, pale wood, matte stone, teal-cyan floor tiles, a small canary). Do NOT copy the reference's content: no homepage headline, no full office diorama, no logo strip, no model shelf.

This page is "The Walkthrough": the booking page for a free, pitch-free, roughly one-hour conversation with Nick (Birdcar), a systems engineer who builds tools for established service businesses. Within three business days of the conversation the visitor receives a written report they keep: what's happening, what I recommend, and where I'd start. The visitor's job on this page: understand the offer and book a time.

STRUCTURE, in reading order (the page is organized by the fair questions an owner asks before booking):
1. Header, about 80px, exactly as the reference.
2. First viewport, two columns.
LEFT column (x 80 to 620): headline about 64px, ink, two lines: "An hour on the work. A report you can use." A paragraph at about 19px, ink-soft: "In a free Walkthrough, you spend about an hour showing me the work that's giving you trouble. Within three business days you get my recommendations in writing." Then the canary-yellow primary button "Book a free Walkthrough →" and a small muted line: "About an hour with me. A written report within three business days. Free."
RIGHT column (x 690 to 1460, y 120 to 960): the dominant element, a large index of four questions stacked as full-width rows separated by thin hairlines. Each row has the question set big and bold at about 34px on the left, a one-sentence answer at about 17px beneath it, and at the row's right end a small premium matte isometric miniature thumbnail on transparent ground. Row 1: "What do I get?" / "A written report within three business days: what's happening, what I recommend, and where I'd start." / thumbnail: a slim bound report booklet with a canary-yellow tab. Row 2: "Is it a pitch?" / "No. If you want to talk about hiring me, you'll bring it up, not me." / thumbnail: a small canary sitting on a desk facing an empty chair. Row 3: "Is it really free?" / "Yes. The conversation and the written report are free." / thumbnail: an open brass birdcage. Row 4: "Is it a fit?" / "It works when I can talk to the people doing the work." / thumbnail: two small desks with figures side by side. The first row sits slightly raised on a white card to show it is the one being read.
3. Bottom band (y 960 to 1024): the top of the next section on white, a heading "Here's how it works."

ART DIRECTION: one dominant move, the question index; the thumbnails are small and consistent, never competing. Direct, calm, premium, adult. Not cute, no toy proportions. No purple, no gradient orbs, no robots, no AI imagery, no stock photos, no prices, no fake metrics, no testimonials. Preserve all quoted words exactly. Treat it as a finished, shippable website.
